Extra notes:
Popeye the Sailor Meets Sindbad the Sailor (1936) was selected for preservation in the National Film Registry in 2004 by the Library of Congress as being "culturally, historically, or aesthetically significant". The print which the Library of Congress has of this short can be viewed on their YouTube channel: Popeye the Sailor Meets Sindbad the Sailor - YouTube

Several of the black and white Popeye shorts, including those in public domain, were later colorized in the 1980's through redrawing every other frame of the shorts and adding color to them. These versions were commissioned by Ted Turner for airing on Cartoon Network.

All of the Famous Studios Popeye shorts have never been officially released on home video to date, and have only been released through unofficial public domain VHS and DVD releases.

All shorts were originally made by Fleischer Studios and Famous Studios, and distributed by Paramount Pictures, but are all now in the public domain.

items.title: All public domain Walt Disney Studios cartoons
items.description:
This is a complete collection of all cartoon shorts made by Walt Disney Studios after 1928 which have fallen in the public domain, meaning that they are free to use and distribute. Many of the shorts which have fallen in the public domain were originally made for the governments of the United States and Canada to encourage viewers to support the war. These shorts include Education for Death (1943), which described the horrible conditions of Nazi Germany during World War II, and The Spirit of  '43 (1943), which is noteworthy for being one of the few shorts starring Donald Duck to fall into the public domain.

A couple noteworthy shorts which do not fall under the WWII category include The Mad Doctor (1933) (one of very few shorts starring Mickey Mouse to fall in the public domain), Susie the Little Blue Coupe (1952), The Cookie Carnival (1935), and Hooked Bear (1956), among a few others. 

Most notably, Steamboat Willie (1928), the first cartoon to feature Mickey Mouse and the first cartoon to utilize sound, entered the public domain in the United States on January 1st, 2024. While it was public domain in the rest of the world for much longer, it was still under copyright in the United States up until that date due to several lawsuits brought on by Disney relating to the subject of extending the copyright of that particular short.

Here is a list of all the shorts which have fallen into the public domain:

Steamboat Willie (1928) - first cartoon short to utilize sound, first Mickey Mouse cartoon, preserved at the National Film Registry in the Library of Congress

The Gallopin' Gaucho (1928) - later digitally colorized through computers for television

Plane Crazy (1928) - released as both sound and silent versions

Minnie's Yoo Hoo (1930)

The Mad Doctor (1933) - later digitally colorized through computers for television

The Cookie Carnival (1935)

The Thrifty Pig (1941)

All Together (1942)

Out of the Frying Pan Into the Firing Line (1942)

Donald's Decision (1942)

The Spirit of '43 (1943)

Education for Death (1943)

The Winged Scourge (1943)

Cleanliness Brings Health (1945)

Susie the Little Blue Coupe (1952)

Hooked Bear (1956)


Extra notes:
Steamboat Willie (1928), the first Mickey Mouse cartoon and the first cartoon to utilize sound, had an odd copyright status in the United States up until 2024. While the short was in the public domain in the rest of the world, it was under copyright in the United States until 2024 due to several lawsuits brought on by Disney relating to the subject of extending the copyright of that particular short. On January 1st, 2024, the short fully entered the public domain, as did the version of Mickey Mouse seen in that short.

items.title: Archie's Weird Mysteries (Full DiC Series) DVD Rip x265 HEVC
items.description:
All 40 episodes of DiC's single-season show "Archie's Weird Mysteries," obtained from the 4-disc DVD set. This set has been out of print since at least 2017, possibly 2012. Seemingly due to the recent Riverdale & Sabrina-influenced Archie boom, these DVDs list for between $50-450 on the secondary market. These are HEVC encodes I derived in HandBrake from a torrent. Some interlacing/banding seems endemic to the DVD that could not be removed.

Developed jointly by DiC in Burbank & their French subsidiary "Les Studios Tex" (itself named after American animator Tex Avery), the show complied with FCC educational programming guidelines. It was stationed on the quasi-education-focused "PAX" network, now known as "Ion," from October of 1999 to February of 2000. It has subsequently aired in syndication on several networks in the ensuing decades, with large lapses in availability. These files are hosted here for purely archival purposes at no gain.

items.title: Batman: The Animated Series - Full Series
items.description: Batman: The Animated Series (Often shortened as Batman TAS or BTAS is an American superhero animated television series based on the DC Comics superhero Batman. Dveloped by Bruce Timm and Eric Radomski, and produced by Warner Bros. Animation, it originally aired on Fox Kids from September 5, 1992 to September 15, 1995 with a total of 85 episodes. After the series ended its original run, a follow-up titled The New Batman Adventures began airing on Kids' WB in 1997 as a continuation of the series, featuring a revamped animation style. Lasting 24 episodes, it has often been included in the same syndicated re-run packages and home media releases. The New Batman Adventures is included. items.title: Bugs Bunny - All This and Rabbit Stew
items.description:
All This and Rabbit Stew is a one-reel animated cartoon short subject in the Merrie Melodies series, produced in Technicolor and released to theatres on September 20, 1941 by Warner Bros. and Vitaphone. It was produced by Leon Schlesinger and directed by an uncredited Tex Avery, with musical supervision by Carl W. Stalling

The cartoon was the final Avery-directed Bugs Bunny short to be released. Although it was produced before The Heckling Hare (after the production of which Avery was suspended from the Schlesinger studio and defected to Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer), it was released afterwards. The title is a parody of that of All This and Heaven Too. Because the cartoon was released after Avery left Warner Bros., Avery's name does not appear in the credits.[1][2][3][4][5]

After copyright on All This and Rabbit Stew expired in 1969, the film fell into the public domain. The cartoon has been considered highly controversial due to racial stereotyping, which prompted United Artists to withhold this cartoon from syndication a year before it entered the public domain, making it one of the infamous Censored Eleven. The plot has Bugs Bunny hunted by a slow-witted African American hunter who sounds and looks like Stepin Fetchit. (Description source: Wikipedia, CC BY-SA)

Video from https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CgNjXeU5OTk

items.title: Cartoon Network "City"-Era Bumps 2004-2007 [Production Quality]
items.description:
This upload reflects ~250 different commercial bumpers produced for Cartoon Network by Australian VFX powerhouse Animal Logic. The files were obtained in the highest possible quality from the Vimeo account of geoffvster (Animal Logic animation supervisor Geoff Valent), often still including the production slate, timecodes, etc. Most of these were rendered at a stage in the production process wherein the sound was still in flux; many have voice acting but may or may not include sound effects & music is largely absent. The generally nondescriptive production names of the files are unaltered.

These bumps are fondly remembered for the slice-of-life view they provided of interactions between various Cartoon Network characters from different eras, such as Fred Jones of Scooby-Doo! chatting it up with the cast of Megas XLR in their mech at a stoplight. The enticing pervasive illusion of the network as a living, breathing place where cartoon characters resided & spent time in each other's company while going about their lives preceded similar concepts such as Space Jam 2's "Metaverse" (which as a fellow Warner Bros. product included many of the same characters, albeit in brief cameos generally without voice acting or any meaningfully apparent personality). At one point in time according to Valent the bumps were pitched to be adapted as an independent television program, but this never materialized for unclear reasons.

Several hundred bumps are thought to exist, making this page in the wider scope of things a relatively poor representation of the era. This defunct & unfortunately non-archived Kametsu thread allegedly contained a veritable trove of 616+ bumpers, many of which were geoffvster's high-quality uploads remuxed with finished audio as-aired. If you have these removed bumpers or other high-quality sources of bumps not archived here, please contact me.

These videos are presented for historical purposes only, being (like most old advertisements) unavailable for any sort of streaming or purchase. These interstitials have been off the air totally in the network's home country since 2007 with other territories dropping the bumps at different times; at the latest they ceased airing in Latin America circa 2010. Neither myself nor the Internet Archive benefit materially in any way from these uploads.

This excerpt consists mainly of Tom and Jerry from Cartoon Network, classic MGM shorts and Popeye from Boomerang, and some episodes of Tom and Jerry Tales from Kids WB. I originally had an episode of She-Ra and an episode of the Super Mario Bros. Super Show on the tape that I recorded from a DVD, but my DVD recorder detected this somehow and edited them out. You might notice the first couple seconds of each. 

A special note:
When I was making these cartoon tapes that I've been uploading lately it was the late 2000s, and I had digital cable and DVR. Hence, I was able to edit, and put things in the order I wanted them in. For most people DVR was a replacement for the VCR, but I realized the full potential of using DVR to make VHS recordings. Most VHS rips you see online are of the "pressed record and left the room for a few hours" variety. Mine are like mixtapes. One might accuse them of being "fake" if they're used to VHS tapes from the 90s, but this is just what's literally on the VHS tapes, copied onto a blank DVD. I honestly don't even know what the point would be of going through the trouble of making a fake video and posting it here. It's not like I'm making money doing this.

You won't see it on this tape in particular, but in the 2010s, I figured out how to run an AV cord from my Playstation 3 to a VCR and record straight from YouTube. This was just for fun really. I would record over stuff on the tapes with YouTube footage, cartoons or things like that. You would probably notice the different aspect ratio on the parts where I did this. Again, not on this particular tape though.

If you're still disappointed in this video or others after my lengthy explanation, I guess I'll have to refund you.

items.description:
Down and Dirty Duck, promoted under the abbreviated title Dirty Duck, is a 1974 American adult animated comedy film written and directed by Charles Swenson and starring Mark Volman and Howard Kaylan (Flo & Eddie) as the voices of a strait-laced, low-level white-collar worker named Willard and an unnamed duck, among other characters. The plot consists of a series of often abstract sequences, including plot material created by stars Kaylan, Volman, Robert Ridgely, and, according to the film's ending credits, various people Swenson encountered during the making of the film.


Dirty Duck received mostly negative reviews, with many criticizing it for its crude humor and others seeing the film as an attempt to cash in on the success of Ralph Bakshi's Fritz the Cat. The film fared better on home video and is now considered a cult film

items.title: Evolved Virtual Creatures
items.description: This narrated computer animation shows results from a research project involving simulated Darwinian evolutions of virtual block creatures. A population of several hundred creatures is created within a supercomputer, and each creature is tested for their ability to perform a given task, such the ability to swim in a simulated water environment. The successful survive, and their virtual genes containing coded instructions for their growth, are copied, combined, and mutated to make offspring for a new population. The new creatures are again tested, and some may be improvements on their parents. As this cycle of variation and selection continues, creatures with more and more successful behaviors can emerge. The creatures shown are results the final products from many independent simulations in which they were selected for swimming, walking, jumping, following, and competing for control of a green cube.

Unlike the Original Star Wars Trilogy, Song of the South, and many others, Fantasia never got the same love. So over the years I took it upon myself to find a way to change that.

Ladies and gentlemen, boys and girls, children of all ages, I present to you something that is not only long overdue, but also making its Internet debut! Disney’s timeless classic Fantasia with Fantasound, Deems Taylor’s voice, AND all the censored scenes restored!

As most of you may know, in what is probably one of the earliest cases of cartoon censorship in the name of political correctness, the “offensive” scenes from the Pastoral Symphony of Fantasia were cut out in 1969, never to be seen in official form again. Additionally, Fantasound was lost to time.

In the early 90s Disney would recreate Fantasound theatrically in two theaters, one in New York and one in Los Angeles. This would be dubbed as “Fantasound 90”. And this would be the basis of the audio in the VHS, Laserdisc, and soundtrack CD released in the early 90s. Although a few seconds of audio is missing from the Pastoral Symphony of those releases due to the censorship. Regarding the intros, these home releases use the shortened (and generally more preferred) intros by Deems Taylor.

In 2000, Disney released Fantasia on DVD. This was dubbed “original and uncut” on the cover. Was it uncut? Debatable. It PANNED the “offensive” scenes (thus yielding complete audio at least) but it is anything but “original” as Disney blatantly falsely advertised on the front cover. Additionally, unlike the LD, the DVD audio is far gone from Fantasound. To boot, Disney chose to use the longer intros. In itself perhaps not necessarily a bad thing as some might prefer that. But the audio of said intros were so deteriorated that they couldn’t be used. So rather than work with what was still usable, Disney decided to completely dub Deems Taylor’s voice entirely with that of actor Corey Burton.

Here is a youtube comparison of the uncensored Pastoral Symphony segment compared to the modern-day censored versions: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gyPFibRadto

In 2010 Fantasia was released on blu ray and its audio was even more far gone from Fantasound than the DVD release (and of course retained the dubbing and censorship of the DVD release).

Another “feature” of both the DVD and blu ray releases is the visual “retouching” that Disney is infamous for when it comes to their older films. Meaning the laserdisc more so reflects the work of the original artists than the more modern releases do.

Now there have been projects on the Internet that have restored all the censored scenes back into Fantasia. But all those releases use the DVD or blu ray release as the basis. Meaning there has yet to be a fully authentic version of Fantasia that is available, officially or otherwise. That is up until February 2021!

Over the years I had collected many Fantasia related things, these include but are not limited to:

In December 2018, I was given (by someone who has long disappeared) a great looking HD version of the censored scenes.

In August 2020, Myspleen.com user AlanGrant released a wonderful rip of the early 90s CAV laserdisc. Here is his write up of it, and I quote:

__start__

This is the 1990 remaster of Fantasia transferred from the CAV LaserDisc boxset, released in January of 1991. This serves not only as a preservation of the 1990 remaster, but of the LaserDisc itself as this is one of numerous disc sets that has disc rot issues which will intensify with time.

Several noticeable differences to other, more modern releases include:

-Color timing is much brighter, especially in the "Nutcracker Suite" section of the film

-A recreation of the 1940 intermission card is used as a title, as opposed to the 1941 "RKO" titlecard used for the 81-minute cut and all post-2000 releases

-Alternate shots with the orchestra in darkness are used for Taylor's narration; later cuts restore Taylor's speaking footage

-Deems Taylor's narration, which was replaced by an actor's redub in post-2000 releases of the film due to deteriorated optical soundtracks

-A ~115 minute runtime made to resemble the 1946 release of the film (which restored Toccata and Fugue), as opposed to the 124-minute 1940 Roadshow version

-An end credits sequence, which all other versions lack

This boxset suffers laser rot to some degree due to the glue used; thankfully here, it's contained to the very beginning of each side. It will be most noticeable in the beginning of the film but each subsequent disc/side has less visual "disc rot".

Transferred using a DVL-90 player, DMR-ES15 passthrough to an AJA Kona LHe card using the S-video input.

Captured as a raw image sequence which was then ran through QTGMC and exported as a 10-bit 4.2.2 H.264 video through ffmpeg (Placebo setting).

(The film runs at 59.94p to better preserve the LaserDisc image as the high framerate and raw modulated image combine to create a "clearer" picture to the eye.)

Digital audio track piped from the DVL-90 to an X-fi Titanium card, bit-matched and recorded as a 44100Hz 16-bit PCM; the file is directly muxed to the .mkv.

Analogue audio was transferred using the AJA KONA LHe card and exported as a monaural Opus file.

Captions were transferred by way of DVD burning on the Panasonic DMR-ES15, ripped using MakeMKV/MKVCleaver and corrected to the .mkv timing in SubtitleEdit.

Chapter stops and titles are direct from the "Chapter Index" insert in the CAV boxset.

__end__

So here I had the most authentic looking and sounding version of Fantasia that Disney put out (ie a HQ LD rip), I had a great looking clip of the censored scenes, among other things.

After many attempts of trying and failing to find someone with the necessary skills and patience to insert the scenes back into the LD and patch up the missing LD audio, on comes user Starbond9 of originaltrilogy.com. I sent him all Fantasia related materials I had collected over the years, and he did a fantastic job. To summarize, he reinserted all the “offensive” scenes into the LD, he patched up the missing audio of the stereo/Fantasound track with that of the DVD audio (the next closest thing we have to Fantasound after the LD), and he patched up the missing audio of the mono track with audio from his own vinyl record!

Here is his write up on what he did, and I quote:

__start__

-Added 5 individual scenes featuring Sunflower and Otica (the centaurette who assists Bacchus)

-Sources on these clips are the audioless HD clips floating around online, color adjusted for LD (adjusted by originaltrilogy.com member BN). The scene with the carpet was from a personal source found on the internet

-3 of said clips were inserted by removing panned/zoomed/and looped existing animations

-2 clips required expanding the video track and inserting a stereo and mono dub as the audio tracks of the movie were physically shortened, see below. (this is also heard on the 1990 CD and Legacy Collection versions of Pastoral)

-Used the DVD stereo audio track as dub source for the missing Fantasound track. These few seconds are NOT Dolby Prologic so listeners with the setting will notice a loss of spatial surround when the two dub spots play. Regular stereo listeners will not notice an issue

-Used a personal copy of a 1961 Mono LP of Pastoral as the dub source for the mono audio track

-Adjusted chapter and subtitles beyond the Pastoral Sunflower clip insert to match the ~8 second shift

-Technical: demuxed individual tracks, remuxed with MKVtoolnix, project assembled in Vegas Pro 14

__end__

I would like to thank him for his time and effort, and for finally bringing an authentic version of Fantasia that showcases, in all its glory, all three of Fantasound, Deems Taylor’s voice, AND the full video/audio of the Pastoral Symphony.

Hopefully someone can also use these two patched up audio tracks for any future Fantasia projects, such as HD 35mm film scans or edits of the blu ray footage.

Please feel free to release this on Torrent, my only request is you keep this write up along with it.

items.title: Fat Albert and the Cosby Kids - The Complete Series
items.description:
In Fat Albert and the Cosby Kids, a young, spirited, obese boy, "Fat Albert Jackson," lives life with his friends, Bill, Russell, Mushmouth, (Ol' Weird) Harold, Bucky, (Dumb) Donald, and Rudy. Together, they love to play games and make music, while learning lessons along the way. Starring Bill Cosby- the "narrator." Every episode-- except for the pilot-- has Bill doing live-action "wraparounds" to guide the audience into the show's lesson. The series is based on his childhood living in North Philadelphia in the 1940's and 50's.

Unfortunately, the same thing that happened with other modern releases of old Filmation cartoons also happened with this series. (Some) DVD releases of the show (especially the 2012 "complete series" one) contained sped-up and high pitched episodes. Every episode has been slowed down 4% and restored to it's correct NTSC speed and pitch. Additionally, I also took the liberty of trying to upscale the audio using a digital audio workstation, because the DVD prints sound horrible. Not every episode sounds perfect, because artifacts and compression are just baked into the masters, but I think I did a pretty good job of making it sound presentable. As for quality, it varies from episode to episode. This cartoon needs a modern-day studio remaster where cels are rescanned, but I think the original source doesn't look too bad. 

It's worth noting that this show went through multiple changes during it's 13-year run:

  • The first four seasons of the show are known as Fat Albert and the Cosby Kids. In these 36 episodes, there's a song at the end (except for two). Ran from 1972-1973 and 1975-1976. During this era, the show covered typical day-to-day problems like meeting new people ("The Stranger"), going to the hospital ("Hospital"), and getting stage fright ("Stage Fright"). However, the series wasn't afraid to cover more serious topics like Marijuana ("Mr. Big Time") and death ("Shuttered Window").
  • Seasons 5-7 were classified as The New Fat Albert Show, featuring the Brown Hornet. Here, the Junkyard Band musical numbers were dropped completely (which was a rather controversial move to many diehard fans), and the show also ramped up a little, covering more serious topics, including child abuse ("Spare the Rod"), gambling ("Heads or Tails?"), and alcohol addiction ("Watch That First Step!"). This "revival" of sorts ran from 1979-1981.
  • Season 8, which premiered in syndication in 1984, is known as The Adventures of Fat Albert and the Cosby Kids. For some reason, Wikipedia says the laugh track and Brown Hornet segments were dropped, but neither is true. The laugh track stays intact, and Brown Hornet appears in multiple episodes. A new segment was added called Legal Eagle. Since this season aired in syndication, it meant they could cover even more serious topics, including prison ("Busted!"), street gangs ("Gang Wars"), and racism ("Long Live the Queen"). Ran from 1984-1985.

FUN FACTS:

  • The writer for the "Junkyard Band" song segments, Ed Fournier, would write all of the season's songs in one day. They were also recorded in the span of one day, with vocals coming from Michael Gray (NOT Bill Cosby)-- who would dub his lines separately. Apparently, one of the musicians said they have tapes of the studio recording the songs, and I would REALLY like to see that one day, because I am super into the Junkyard Band segments (the musician who said that has since passed in early 2022).
  • Despite airing on CBS for over 10 years, Fat Albert and the Cosby Kids moved to NBC in 1989, where it would air reruns, to little fanfare. Reruns also aired on USA Network's Cartoon Express in 1988. Later, in 2011, BOUNCETV would acquire the rights to the cartoon, airing it in primetime and early mornings up until mid-2018, where the show was removed permanently. The show stayed on the schedule despite the Cosby allegations. I included two BOUNCE airings ("Wheeler" and "Faking the Grade") in the collection.
  • A typical episode of the show would cost around $80,000-85,000 to produce, which, adjusted for inflation (2026), would equate to around $600,000-650,000.
  • It would take around four months to produce an episode of Fat Albert, from concept to final production.

ALSO INCLUDED IN THIS COLLECTION:

  • Fat Albert's Easter, Halloween, and Christmas specials.
  • The 1969 pilot ("Hey, Hey, Hey, It's Fat Albert!), and
  • The 1971 pilot ("The Great Go-Cart Race" AKA "The Weird Harold Special"). This special was produced in 1971 but didn't air until 1973-- on NBC, for some reason.
  • The alternate versions of "Shuttered Window" and "Junk Food," featuring the Brown Hornet. Apparently, there are more episodes that have "alternate versions," released on the Time Life video compilations and aired in syndication. I don't own any of the Time Life releases, so you might have to wait a little on that one. I have yet to upload the Brown Hornet segment from "An Ounce of Prevention," but plan to do so in the future.
  • Additionally, there are also allegedly episodes (season 2 ones) that had Bill RE-RECORD his live-action segments in 1984 for the syndication season. Again, haven't come across any of them. Except for the episode "The Newcomer."
  • A 45-minute documentary special, with commentary from Bill Cosby and others on how Fat Albert came to be-- and the impact it had.
  • "Food For Thought," an episode that was meant for schools only, and was never broadcasted on television. This was produced around 1981, so the sixth/seventh season of the show. 
  • The uncensored version of "Busted!" featuring the original dialogue before the episode was edited. This version of the episode contains mild swearing and implied r*pe from the inmates. I can't even believe we have this to begin with, this is insanely rare.
  • The never-before-seen, in-house "Attention Study" versions of the first two episodes of The New Fat Albert Show (but, as you can see if you watch them, the revival was originally titled The New Adventures of Fat Albert) These attention studies were used after the episode had been produced to understand where in the episode the kids' attention spans would drop off for future reference.
  • Shortened versions of episodes, used for schools. These shortened episodes removed the laugh track completely, cut some songs down and removed key scenes to reach the 15-minute mark.

NOTE: For some reason, the laugh track is completely absent on about six episodes. I assume this was just a print/mastering problem, because the laugh track is intact on all of those episodes on the Teletoon Retro encodes, especially of The New Fat Albert Show. The absence of the laugh track causes some pretty awkward silences in-between dialogue, and sometimes, it's just radio silent. So if anyone wants me to replace those with the Teletoon Retro versions that have the laugh tracks, just tell me.

At the end of the day, until we get a streaming/Blu-Ray release (WITH THE CORRECT SPEED), this is the best we have. So cheer on, all you Fat Albert fans, feast to your heart's content. Hey, hey, hey!

items.title: Flip The Frog - Fiddlesticks
items.description: The following concise, informative description was taken from http://en.wikipedia.org: Flip the Frog was Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer's first sound cartoon. It is about a happy-go-lucky, needy frog, named Flip the Frog. This cartoon was created by Ub Iwerks in 1930. He had drawn a frog and his girlfriend in "Night'", one of the last Silly Symphonies short films he drew while working for Walt Disney. After leaving Disney, Ub Iwerks began the Flip cartoon series with the help of Pat Powers. The first cartoon that Ub Iwerks made for the series was called Fiddlesticks (released on August 16, 1930), and it was also the first color sound cartoon ever made. Fiddlesticks was made in two-color Technicolor. The rest of the Flip series were made in black and white, except for Techno-Cracked (1933). FIDDLESTICKS is perhaps the least funny and entertaining of the FLIP cartoons, many of which have surprisingly adult gags.

The show is similar to fellow Ruegger-led programs such as Animaniacs, and the humor is unique in its inclusions of slapstick, fourth wall firings, parody, surreal humor and pop cultural references. items.description:
H.R. Pufnstuf ★ Complete TV Series - with Sheet Music and Coloring Book Bonus! Includes the original 17 Episodes: plus the Pufnstuf Movie, and a Pufnstuf Satire Video. Groovy!!!

Reviewer bronx72 posted on March 24th, 2026: "Also that you can still thank Sid Krofft himself on Instagram:
https://www.instagram.com/sidkrofft?igsh=MjFnOHJ3Y2NzdTQy
I still have a 45 we sent away for. Good times; happy memories; artistic inspiration for a lifetime. :-)  😃 "
Many thanks to bronx72 for sharing this information. As soon as I read their review: I reposted their tip, up here, for everyone to enjoy. Unfortunately, Sid Krofft died just 17 days after that review was posted, and it is a Legacy Page now.

This Page is In Memory of Sid (Died: April 10th, 2026) and Marty (Died: November 25th, 2023) Krofft - their Imagination escaped their heads … and invaded the heads of generations of kids, Young and Old alike!




A Sid and Marty Krofft Saturday Morning TV show from the late 60's and early 70's.
These materials are made available under a "Fair Use" provision of Copyright Law - as significant cultural and historical video artifacts: and are for free personal use only!


Much to my delight: I stumbled upon the trainwreck, of the corpses, of three DVDs. The archivist that uploaded them has a very unusual method of disassembling multiple DVDs and stacking the like pieces from all of them together in different heaps … I assure you that this jumbles them up very thoroughly. I was only delighted because I had just figured out a method, to finally recover the master videos, from another series of eight DVDs - that were also very completely jumbled up by the same person.

I got this series of 52 videos out of that last batch of Scrambled Up DVDs: https://archive.org/details/shadow-raiders That DVD set had two different languages: and I got both recovered.

I just found the old 1969 TV Series H. R. Pufnstuff … all thoroughly mixed together (like I said: it is a trainwreck). But now I'm getting better at recovery, from this archivist's … rather unique … way of backing up DVDs - not as ISO Images but as Stacks of Files (all named the same), - and I turned the unwatchable mess on the source page of https://archive.org/details/h.r.-pufnstuf into this page - with a complete TV series: ready for you to enjoy.

This DVD set has no subtitles or alternate languages - just 17 episodes of nostalgic goodness (or pure camp: from a bygone era) … and an unexpected find of a H. R. Pufnstuf picture, and coloring, and song book: with the sheet music AND lyrics to Twelve of the original Songs of the TV series (perhaps written by Sid and Marty Krofft themselves?) - you could play and/or sing along!!! 
It says on the Cover: "Three books in one … Coloring Book / Photo Book / Song Book.   West Coast Publications, INC.  Star Series 29  $2.95" (That was in 1969 Dollars)
Videos … with Song Sheet Music on the Same Page - to a few of the songs in the videos: this is the Only One in my Video Collection! 
https://archive.org/download/h_r_pufnstuf/pufnstuf_coloring_song_book.pdf

I got a copy of "The Pufnstuf Movie" from this page: https://archive.org/details/H.R.Pufnstuf and if you want to see more Pufnstuf, or Jack Wild (Oliver!), videos: you need to go check that huge collection out!!! Many many more hours of great videos!!

I also found (on YouTube), and posted, a Lo-Rez copy of the Satire done about the show - but please do not watch that last forbidden video. It will rot your mind. And it is a popular lie: " … I can't speak to what adults were doing when they were watching the shows. We just set out to make a quality children's program". Sadly, Marty Krofft DID Not create under the influence (Sid … who knows?). It's just a kid's puppet show: gone rogue.

These videos actually have historic, as well as entertainment, value. Think about it: nothing from the 1970's - or Later - can be seen in here. 
This is a video Time Capsule of 1969 … how it looked then / how it sounded / how they did things fifty five years ago. And at least one review posted testifies to the lifelong joy and inspiration given by the Krofft Brothers to a generation of kids - they DID Change lives! What a legacy to leave behind!

I found a video right here on the Archive about the career and lives of Sid and Marty Krofft and it's pretty good! If you like this series and want to learn more about how it came about / how it was made / and insider details about it, go watch:
E True Hollywood Story S04E49 H.R. Pufnstuf The Strange World Of Sid & Marty Krofft at https://archive.org/details/e-true-hollywood-story-s04e49-h.r.-pufnstuf-the-strange-world-of-sid-and-marty-krofft

I laughed hard at the automatic O.C.R. translation … of sheet music: https://archive.org/stream/h_r_pufnstuf/pufnstuf_coloring_song_book_djvu.txt - oh, it got some of the lyrics correct, no doubt - but the stuff between the printed lines of text was making it swallow it's tongue, and turn blue - trying hard to "Read" it! (The NOTES look like "ALL b's, O's, and d's"!! Are you SURE this is in English?!?)  I tried reading it's output text / spasm: and laughed for several minutes!!! "Tease a Computer" and this brilliant alphanumeric salad is about what you should expect!!!

No, haven't gotten all of the bugs out of it yet. Still a ways to go. But there HAS been progress …

What you are getting here (From Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H.R._Pufnstuf# ):

H.R. Pufnstuf is a children's television series produced by Sid and Marty Krofft in the United States. It was the first Krofft live-action, life-sized-puppet program (not including their previous work with the Hanna-Barbera program The Banana Splits Adventure Hour). The seventeen episodes were originally broadcast Saturday mornings from September 6, 1969, to December 27, 1969.

In 2004 and 2007, H.R. Pufnstuf was ranked #22 and #27 respectively on TV Guide's Top Cult Shows Ever.

Overview:
The Kroffts created the H.R. Pufnstuf character for the HemisFair '68 World's Fair, where they produced a show called Kaleidoscope for the Coca-Cola pavilion. The character's name was Luther, and he became a mascot for the fair. (T.I.L.)

H.R. Pufnstuf introduced the Kroffts' most-used plot scenario of a fairy tale of good versus evil, as well as their second plot scenario of the stranger in a strange land. The show centered on a shipwrecked boy named Jimmy, portrayed by teenage actor Jack Wild. He is 11 years old when he arrives on the island and turns 12 in the episode called "The Birthday Party." Jimmy and a talking flute named Freddy take a ride on a mysterious boat, but the boat is actually owned by a wicked witch named Wilhelmina W. Witchiepoo (portrayed by Billie Hayes) who rides on a broomstick-vehicle called the Vroom Broom. She uses the boat to lure Jimmy and Freddy to her castle on Living Island, where she intends to take Jimmy prisoner and steal Freddy for her own purposes.

The Mayor of Living Island is a friendly and helpful anthropomorphic dragon named H.R. Pufnstuf, performed by Roberto Gamonet and voiced by the show's writer Lennie Weinrib, who also voiced many of the other characters. The dragon rescues Jimmy and protects him from Witchiepoo, as his cave is the only place where her magic has no effect.

All of the characters on Living Island were realized by large, cumbersome costumes or puppetry of anthropomorphic animals and objects. Everything was alive on the island, including houses, boats, clocks, candles, and so forth; virtually any part of the Living Island sets could become a character, usually voiced in a parody of a famous film star such as Mae West, Edward G. Robinson, or John Wayne.

Production:
After creating costumes for characters in the live-action portion of The Banana Splits Adventure Hour, Sid and Marty Krofft were asked to develop their own Saturday morning children's series for NBC. The plot was recycled from Kaleidoscope, a live puppet show the Kroffts had staged in the Coca-Cola pavilion of the HemisFair '68 World's Fair. It included several key characters from this show, such as Luther the dragon and a silly witch. Other ideas were cultivated from Sid's life. As a child, he had charged friends buttons, not pennies, to view puppet shows in his back yard; buttons were standard currency on Living Island. Sid and Marty had toured with their puppets as the opening act for Judy Garland, and they based Judy the Frog on her. Ludicrous Lion bears more than a passing resemblance to Irving, the eponymous lion in a pilot they had made in 1957 called Here's Irving.

Sid's friend Lionel Bart asked him to view a rough cut of the movie adaptation of Oliver! Sid took notice of young actor Jack Wild and immediately decided that he was the kid whom he wanted to play the lead in his television series. Only two actresses auditioned to play Witchiepoo. The first was then-unknown Penny Marshall. Stage veteran Billie Hayes came in next, set into a maniacal cackle and hopped up on a desk. She was given the part on the spot.



Much more detail about the show is revealed at Wikipedia, and was omitted for brevity: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H.R._Pufnstuf# Read all about it.

A 1960's Time Capsule!!! ☮︎ Groovy!!! ✌🏻




Episodes:

01    "The Magic Path"            September 6, 1969
Jimmy and H. R. Pufnstuf infiltrate Witchiepoo's castle to rescue Judy Frog so that they can get directions to the Magic Path. The Magic Path is the only way off Living Island. Will Jimmy and Freddy get back home?

02    "The Wheely Bird"           September 13, 1969
Jimmy and H. R. Pufnstuf use a bird-shaped "Trojan Horse" as a ruse to enter Witchipoo's castle and recover Freddy from Witchiepoo.

03    "Show Biz Witch"            September 20, 1969
When shyster Ludicrous Lion convinces Jimmy that he has a super-duper pogo stick for sale that could bounce him home, H. R. Pufnstuf and Jimmy conduct a talent show to raise the money.

04    "The Mechanical Boy"         September 27, 1969
After catching him trying to steal her boat, Witchiepoo puts a spell on Jimmy that turns him into a mechanical boy and commands him to acquire Freddy for her. The Clock People have to find a way to cure Jimmy.

05    "The Stand In"              October 4, 1969
When H. R. Pufnstuf's sister Shirley comes to Living Island to make a movie, Jimmy and Freddie get parts in it. Together, they hatch a plot to get Witchiepoo into the movie so that Jimmy can steal her Vroom Broom to escape.

06    "The Golden Key"             October 11, 1969
Jimmy buys a map to the location of the Golden Key which unlocks the Golden Door (a secret way off of Living Island), Witchiepoo captures H. R. Pufnstuf and imprisons him in her dungeon diverting Jimmy from his escape.

07    "The Birthday Party"         October 18, 1969
It's Jimmy's birthday and Pufnstuf and his friends fix a surprise birthday party for him. Witchiepoo invites herself to Jimmy's party and steals Freddy by rendering the partygoers helpless with laughing gas.

08    "The Box Kite Kaper"         October 25, 1969
Jimmy and Freddy attempt to fly from Living Island in a giant box kite during a kite-flying contest.

09      "You Can't Have Your Cake"    November 1, 1969
Witchiepoo hides in a cake to steal Freddy. Also, Judy Frog teaches the gang a pre-Michael Jackson Moonwalk dance.

10 "The Horse with the Golden Throat"    November 8, 1969
The Polka-Dotted Horse accidentally swallows Freddy causing a big catastrophe with Dr. Blinky, H. R. Pufnstuf, and Jimmy.

11    "Dinner for Two"            November 15, 1969
Jimmy and Freddy both age 70 years when the Clock Family's time machine malfunctions. Witchiepoo mistakes Jimmy for an old man and
falls in love with him.

12    "Flute, Book and Candle"    November 22, 1969
Freddy gets turned into a mushroom by the touch of Witchiepoo's evil mushrooms. Jimmy disguises himself as a beggar (in the guise of Jack Wild's Artful Dodger character from the 1968 film Oliver!) to rescue Freddy from the spell.

13    "Tooth for a Tooth"          November 29, 1969
Disguised as a little girl, Witchiepoo visits Dr. Blinky about a bad tooth. But she breaks into fits of rage when the pain becomes too much forcing the doctor to calm her down via love potion.

14    "The Visiting Witch"        December 6, 1970
Witchiepoo receives a message from headquarters that the Boss Witch is coming to Living Island for an inspection. In a plot to impress the Boss Witch, she ends up kidnapping H. R. Pufnstuf.

15    "The Almost Election of Witchiepoo"    December 13, 1969
Witchiepoo runs for Mayor of Living Island challenging H. R. Pufnstuf with another of her spells.

16 "Whaddya Mean the Horse Gets the Girl?"    December 21, 1969
H. R. Pufnstuf's sister Shirley stars in a movie to raise money for Living Island's anti-witch fund.

17    "'Jimmy Who?"                  December 27, 1969
Jimmy gets amnesia that Dr. Blinky and Witchiepoo take turns trying to cure with flashbacks from earlier episodes.

18 - Pufnstuf (also known as Pufnstuf Zaps the World) is a 1970 American comedy fantasy musical film produced by Sid and Marty Krofft Enterprises and released by Universal Pictures. It is based on the children's television series H.R. Pufnstuf, a show that features a cast of puppets on a "living island." https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pufnstuf_(film)

19 - Wikipedia:  One of the most notable parodies of H.R. Pufnstuf was "The Altered State of Druggachusetts", a segment on the HBO comedy series Mr. Show with Bob and David. The sketch consists of a failed television pilot for a kids' show introduced by "Sam and Criminy Craffft" (portrayed by Bob Odenkirk and David Cross). The show itself is similar to H.R. Pufnstuf, with drug references made humorously overt. Instead of a talking flute, the boy carries a talking bong (Gandalf), and all of the residents in Druggachusetts take, or are living incarnations of, various drugs (Like Hallucino Genny - who can taste colors!!).

You have to be old to remember watching this as a child. Yeah, that dates me.

Video Size: 640x480

James Bond Jr. is a character described as the nephew of Ian Fleming's spy James Bond. The name was first used in a 1967 spinoff novel, The Adventures of James Bond Junior 003½, authored by the never clarified pseudonym R. D. Mascott. The idea was used again in 1991 in an American animated series starring Bond Jr. The series was mildly successful, spawning a six-volume novelization series by John Peel (writing as John Vincent), a comic book series by Marvel Comics published in 1992, and video games for the Nintendo Entertainment System and Super NES.

items.title: Marvel Super Heroes 1960s Cartoon Series Preservation
items.description: In 1966, Marvel Comics hired animation company Grantray-Laurence to create "The Marvel Superheroes", a series of daily cartoons based on their titles Captain America, Thor, Hulk, Iron Man, and the Sub-Mariner. As it was Marvel's first foray into television animation, the producers stretched out the budget by using existing stories and artwork. Original comic art pages were Xeroxed and used as key frames, with animators adding only mouth and limb animation. Body movement was often accomplished by animating still images across a background.  Fortunately for comic fans, this cost-cutting move preserved for all time the original artwork of Gene Colon, Don Heck, and Jack "King" Kirby, and the dialog of Stan Lee. It was exactly what readers have always asked TV and movie makers to do: just film the comics.  A year later they released the Spider-Man series, with one of the most iconic theme songs ever. While early episodes dealt with the web-slinger's traditional rogue's gallery, later episodes dealt with more generic villains. While Steve Ditko and John Romita Sr did character designs, they were not directly involved in the artwork, and Stan Lee had only a story consultant position, lead

items.title: Maxie's World: The Complete Series
items.description:
Here's is a complete collection of originally syndicated episodes of the original animated series, Maxie's World with the original DiC and Claster Television logos after the end credits and bumpers.

Information
Maxie's World is an American animated children's television series produced by DIC Entertainment. It consists of only one season, comprising a total of 16 half-hour episodes including 32 segments (15 minutes each).

Premise
The series takes place in a fictional seaside town of Surfside, California and follows the adventures of teenager Maxie and her circle of friends. She attends Surfside High School where she is a popular straight "A" student, cheerleader and surfer girl, while after school, she serves as host and investigative reporter of her own eponymous talk show, Maxie's World. 

Through her work as a journalist, she routinely finds herself called upon to investigate mysteries and solve crimes, bringing the villains (criminals and perpetrators) to justice (unlike the Scooby-Doo franchise by Hanna-Barbera). Frequently accompanying Maxie in her adventures is her boyfriend, Rob, a handsome and popular football and soccer star at Surfside High.

Additional members of Maxie's circle of friends include Ashley Wooden, Carly Cooper, and Simone Williams, while male friends, Mushroom and Ferdie routinely provide the series with its slapstick comedy elements. Providing much of the series' conflict is Jeri Jeffries, who is envious of Maxie and is often shown manipulating events to humiliate the TV star in an attempt to sabotage her career and get her own TV show. 

*In addition to the comedy and mystery elements, the series occasionally takes the opportunity to address more serious issues, including eight very special episodes which deals with the issues of divorce, eating disorders (weight obsessions and overeating), vandalism, teenage smoking, stress and fatigue, dropping out of school, the loss of a pet, and shoplifting.

Additionally, the crossover episode, "Beach Blanket Battle", saw the main characters from both Maxie's World and Beverly Hills Teens that compete in a charity fundraising competition.

Episodes
  1. Date Expectations/Ride for Your Life
  2. Wheelie Bad Dudes/The Not-So Great Outdoors
  3. Goodbye Ghoul World/This Rap's for You
  4. To Be or Not to Be Ferdie/Misadventures in Babysitting

  14. Dear Hunk/The Slumber Party

items.title: Mega Man (1994)
items.description:
Mega Man is a science fiction superhero animated television series co-produced by Ruby-Spears Productions and Ashi Productions. It is based on the video game series of the same name by Capcom.[1] The TV series began on September 11, 1994 and ended on January 19, 1996. Two seasons were produced with a third season planned, but the show was cancelled due to budget constraints.

Dr. Light and Dr. Wily were brilliant scientists in the field of robotics, who worked together in a laboratory trying to advance the science. One day, they finished an extremely advanced prototype, but shortly after being activated, it started destroying the laboratory. Dr. Light immediately believed that the prototype's guidance system, which Dr. Wily had personally programmed, was the source of the problem and concluded they would start over again. Angered, Dr. Wily attempted to steal the plans later that night, but Dr. Light catches him. Wily is able to steal the plans after knocking Dr. Light down, and goes off to what is apparently an abandoned area, and modifies the old robot prototype into Proto Man.

Later, Dr. Light builds Rock and Roll, advanced robots with personalities, along with Ice Man, Guts Man, and Cut Man. Dr. Wily and Proto Man go and steal the robots, reprogramming the latter three robots as henchmen. Dr. Wily attempts to reprogram Rock and Roll at his lab later, but Rock decides to trick Dr. Wily. He tells Dr. Wily that Dr. Light also built "super warrior robots", and that if Rock and Roll are let go, he'll tell him how to defeat the robots. Rock uses this lie (Dr. Wily believing robots can't lie) to cause a distraction and escape with Roll. Dr. Light decides to reprogram and reoutfit Rock into Mega Man, who from then on keeps the world safe. This tale is told in Episode 1, "The Beginning".

Throughout the episodes, Mega Man thwarts Wily's various schemes, in a similar fashion to that of the Super Friends, usually ending with Rush acting in similar vein to Scooby-Doo.

items.title: Mr. Men - The Complete Original TV Series
items.description:
Mr. Men - The Complete Original TV Series

Video Size: 720x576

Mr. Men is a series of children's books by English author Roger Hargreaves commencing in 1971. From 1981, an accompanying series of Little Miss books by the same author, but with female characters were published. A similar series of animal characters known as Timbuctoo started in 1978. After Hargreaves's death in 1988, his son Adam Hargreaves began writing and illustrating new Mr. Men and Little Miss stories like Mr. Cool, Mr. Rude, Mr. Good, Little Miss Scary, Little Miss Bad and Little Miss Whoops.

Each book in the original Mr. Men and Little Miss series introduced a different title character and his/her single dominant personality trait to convey a simple moral lesson. The Mr. Men and Little Miss characters frequently reappeared in other characters' books. As of 2015, a total of 85 Mr. Men and Little Miss characters had been featured in the series.The books' simple stories, with brightly coloured, boldly drawn illustrations, made them very popular, with sales of over 100 million worldwide across 28 countries.

items.title: Reading Rainbow - TV Series (1983)
items.description: Reading Rainbow is an American educational children's television series that originally aired on PBS and afterward PBS Kids from July 11, 1983 [1] [2] to November 10, 2006, with reruns continuing to air until August 28, 2009. 155 30-minute episodes were produced over 21 seasons. Before its official premiere, the show aired for test audiences in the Nebraska and Buffalo, New York markets (their PBS member stations, the Nebraska ETV [now Nebraska Public Media] and WNED-TV , respectively, were co-producers of the show). The purpose of the show was to encourage a love of books and reading among children. In 2012, an iPad and Kindle Fire educational interactive book reading and video field trip application was launched bearing the name of the program. The public television series garnered over 200 broadcast awards, including a Peabody Award and 26 Emmy Awards , 10 of which were in the "Outstanding Children's Series" category. [5] The concept of a reading series for children originated with Twila Liggett, PhD who in partnership with Cecily Truett Lancit and Larry Lancit, at Lancit Media Productions in New York created the television series. items.title: ReBoot ★ Complete TV Series with Subtitles and MKV
items.description:
ReBoot ★ Complete TV Series with Subtitles and MKV versions. Subtitles in the video files: both the MKV Files and the MP4 videos. (Subtitles are not in the Three Bonus videos.)

This is the first popular cartoon series, entirely rendered by computers, to gain wide acclaim - and viewing. (I believe Transformers: Beast Wars was the Second such - and Shadow Raiders the Third. All are among my favorites.) This is literally animation history you are watching! Unprecedented at the time: and still very remarkable even today!
I just found it in High Definition elsewhere on the Archive: https://archive.org/details/Reboot-HD Those videos are much better!! 

Go Watch those - or just Download them all right now: (27.3 GB) https://archive.org/compress/Reboot-HD/formats=H.264%20IA&file=/Reboot-HD.zip !


I know THIS has to be one of my favorite animated series of all time. I originally uploaded this from my personal collection. <---- those were poor quality compared to what I now have.  I recovered better videos off of ISO Images from https://archive.org/details/reboot-the-definitive-mainframe-edition - With English Subtitles intact - and replaced the original videos.

On August 29th, 2024 - I uploaded to this page NEW MP4 and MKV videos, with English Subtitles in them - and the playlists were updated. Download the videos and watch them on your device. A couple of those 1st season videos have secondary "Director's Commentary" audio tracks available on them. No Subtitles for the three bonus videos.

The three Bonus Videos from the Extras DVD are included. They play right after the 4th season concludes, or you may jump right to them.
ReBoot Special Bonus 1 Fast Forward - the Making of Reboot  (In 1990 - Bob originally had no lips. He claimed they were stolen … as will be revealed in the first 3 minutes of this Special.)
ReBoot Special Bonus 2 Alphanumeric - Looking Back at Reboot  (It is confirmed that Reboot was the First Fully CGI Show. This is literally animation history you are watching.)
ReBoot Special Bonus 3 Original Presentation and Animated Character Models (The first concept they did - "Enzo's Overwrite Delivery" - turned out to be the Second Episode "Racing the Clock" … here, the birth of that episode is shown.)

The following was retrieved from https://web.archive.org/web/20220602201444/https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0108903/
__________________________________________________________________________
Storyline:
The extraordinary adventures of life within a computer, as depicted in one of the world's first totally-computer-generated series. The riotous humor, infinitely-variable action and scenery, and intelligent use of every computer reference known, combine to produce a stunning universe where good constantly fights the forces of evil. Dot Matrix and her brother Enzo, plus thousands of friendly binomes, live in Mainframe, which is plagued by viruses Megabyte and sister strain Hexadecimal. Guardian Bob is sent from the Net to protect them, and soon makes it his home. Together, they must prevent Megabyte from taking control of all the systems. As an added complication, games being played by the mystical User invade the system regularly, and must be defeated, or else portions of the city are laid waste... This gives us a chance to see every genre of video-game ever conceived, from the point of view of the characters! When Megabyte finally manages to banish Bob, Enzo takes over as the city's Guardian, but things will never be quite the same ...

(They put "Mike the TV" in Charge - and the 'not ready for prime time players' sum up the entirety of Season 3, in a most hilarious "Follow the Bouncing Ball [SCSI]" skit - done to fast paced Gilbert and Sullivan music.)

items.description:
South Park ☆ La Série ☆ VF ☆ 1997-2024

South Park (prononcé : [saʊθ pɑːɹk]) est une série d'animation américaine pour adultes créée et écrite par Trey Parker et Matt Stone, diffusée depuis le 13 août 1997 sur Comedy Central.

La série met en scène les aventures de quatre enfants d'école primaire : Stan Marsh, Kyle Broflovski, Eric Cartman et Kenny McCormick qui vivent à South Park, petite ville du Colorado. Son humour se veut absurde, parodique, sarcastique, graveleux et scatologique, et elle est souvent une critique et une satire de la société américaine. Mais c'est bien son ton très provocateur et ses dialogues souvent grossiers qui la distinguent dans le paysage audiovisuel. Depuis ses débuts, ses auteurs bénéficient d'une très grande liberté assez rare pour une série sur le câble américain.

Bien que controversée, la série est récompensée à de nombreuses reprises, notamment par cinq Emmy Awards, ainsi qu'un Peabody Award. La popularité de la série aboutit, deux ans après ses débuts, à la création du long métrage South Park, le film.

Le 5 août 2021, la série est renouvelée jusqu'en 2027 soit jusqu’à la saison 30 et quatorze téléfilms produits exclusivement pour la plateforme Paramount+ sont prévus.

items.title: Space Angel- Space Hijackers
items.description:
One of the first cartoons made dedicated for the early TV market. In the 1960's animation was an expensive precess costing up to $2,500 a minute to produce. Space Angel cartoons were mostly storyboads where the only movement was the mouths of the characters(Syncro-Vox system). This animation style was similar to Clutch Cargo Cartoons!

 Space Angel was the code name of Scott McCloud, an agent for the Earth Bureau of Investigation. Devoted to the security and welfare of the solar system, McCloud and his crew roamed the universe in the super-spaceship, Starduster. The crew, who made up the bureau's Interplanetary Space Force, included Taurus, an expert pilot and mechanic; Crystal, a specialist in electronics and astro-navigation; and Crystal's father, Professor Mace, head of base station Evening Star.

Many people believe that Taurus the ship's engineer may have been the model for Star Trek's scotty! The similarities bee tween the two characters are just too similar to be a coincidence. 

These Cartoons were run on kid shows in the 1960's! In 1962 when this show was in syndication you could find Space Angel on Kid shows like the Marshal J show http://captainerniesshowboat.com/marshalj.html

Marshal J didn't have a big budget so Space angel, Clutch Cargo and eventually Hanna Barbera cartoons fit the bill perfectly. I have very fond memories of these kid shows and I kind of miss them. So sit back and be a kid again! Enjoy!

items.title: Steamboat Willie (1928)
items.description:
Directed by Walt Disney & Ub Iwerks

Released on November 18, 1928

Though Steamboat Willie was the first cartoon in Mickey's lineup to be released, two cartoons Plane Crazy and The Gallopin' Gaucho were produced before but released after this cartoon.

The title is a parody of the Buster Keaton film, Steamboat Bill, Jr., also released in 1928.

The signature melody for Steamboat Willie has been used as an introduction for movies by Walt Disney Feature Animation ever since the animation studio's restructured by John Lasseter and Ed Catmull under the name Walt Disney Animation Studios (starting with the movie Meet the Robinsons). It starts out as a blank piece of paper as lines are drawn onto it, recreating the iconic scene from a basic sketch to the final iteration.

items.title: Tarzoon, Shame Of The Jungle [1975]
items.description: The feature film debut of noted cartoonist Picha. This bizarre animated oddity was released during a wave of raunchy animated epics after the wild success of Ralph Bakshi's Fritz The Cat. The film is a sendup of old Tarzan films made in the 1930's and concerns Tarzoon [renamed "Shame" in the American version to avoid a lawsuit brought forth by the Burroughs' Estate] a man raised by apes in the jungles of Africa, attempting to rescue his sweetheart June from the bald, multi-breasted queen who wants June for her hair. Tarzoon must combat the elements of the jungle as well as the queen's military consisting of anthropomorphic penises [brought to life in the most unhinged manner possible]. The American English dub was rewritten by Saturday Night Live writers Michael O'Donoghue and Anne Beatts, and features SNL alumnus including Bill Murray and John Belushi in the voice cast. This is true psychotronic cinema at its finest, and is well worth your time if you are at all a fan of raunchy animation of yesteryear as well as the bellylaughs once found on Saturday Night Live.

items.description:
Cleaned up from heavy digital compression faults. A few were fixed against stretched aspect ratios or trimmed from severe edge artifacts.

This upload is the complete set of all episodes for the 1985 series.

Includes generated subtitles.

I claim no credit, ownership, or anything else.

Why did I do things the way I did?
- "MP4? Not MKV?"
 Internet Archive has fairly specific requirements for video uploads in order to play them directly. If those requirements aren't met, then IA automatically re-encodes the videos in question and creates duplicates of every file within the upload page, sometimes very low quality. I encode h.264 in MP4, with AAC Audio and external SRT subtitles to maximize compatibility with the IA video player.
- "Why are the episodes ordered that way?"
I order my episodes based on a particular database for a particular Video streaming app. My ordering matches those 2 things, even if it's incorrect according to other databases or hard chronological air dates. Air dates can be a poor guideline for intended ordering, however - networks frequently got creative with their presentation order, even for first-time showings, because reasons. Who knows with those people...

items.description: THE BRAVE TIN SOLDIER very closely follows the original story by the Brothers Grimm. A one-legged tin soldier is cruelly mocked by other toys because of his deformity. The soldier falls in love with a toy ballerina who is desired by the toy king. The king exercises his military power to get the girl for himself. The tale ends tragically, with a surprisingly graphic execution by firing squad. This is probably too violent and weird for little kids. The cartoon itself is very nicely animated, perhaps even moreso than the other Ub Iwerks fairy tales. There are some celebrity caricature toys, including a Groucho Marx jack-in-the-box. The video transfer of The Brave Tin Soldier is not as good as those of many other Iwerks cartoons, but it's watchable. There are places which appear to have bleed-through from something previously recorded on the same video tape from which the cartoon was transferred.

items.title: The Groovie Goolies Archive
items.description:
Following the success of "The Archie Show" and its companion, "Sabrina the Teenage Witch," Filmation greenlit an original companion for Sabrina based on The Universal Monsters.  "Laugh-In" writers Jack Mendelsohn and Jim Mulligan were hired to develop the show, patterning it after that gag-a-minute series, and musical numbers were added to ape the success of The Archies. The Goolies characters also appeared in more traditional stories on Sabrina's show. "Sabrina and the Groovie Goolies" premiered in the fall of 1970, to great acclaim from children... and to the disdain of parents' groups, who routinely singled the show out for its grotesque characters and comical violence. The next year, the two shows were split apart, never to be reassembled (until now!).

There were a variety of musical groups featured on the show (The Monster Trio, The Mummies and the Puppies, The Spirits of 76, etc.) , but the music all came from the same team, the guys who were also behind the songs on Filmation's "The Hardy Boys" (and there's some musical overlap on their second album, "Wheels," which was released the same year). One of the bands that showed up in preliminary artwork was The Running Stones, a colorful band of rocks with arms, legs, and instruments who were probably replaced by The Rolling Headstones because they looked like insects-- but weirdly, these unused characters were featured in both the American and Japanese coloring books.

As for the music, the masterminds behind it were Richard Delvy, Ed Fournier, and Dick Monda, who copyrighted the songs under the aliases Linda Martin (Delvy), Sherry Gayden/Gaden (Fournier), and Janis Gwinn (Monda). Monda and Fournier appeared as Drac and Frankie on the tie-in album cover (along with Jeffrey Thomas as Wolfie), as well in the live-action portion of The Haunted Heist/Daffy Duck & Porky Pig Meet the Groovie Goolies. 

Not only were the Goolies popular in the USA, but they were wildly successful around the world. In most countries, the dialogue was dubbed but the songs remained in English -- however, that wasn't the case in Japan and Czechoslovakia, where the songs were revised and re-recorded in their native tongue.  In France, the show spent a period as a featured component of the children's anthology "Recré A2." The songs remained in English, but a live-action Goolies band sometimes burst in singing a French variation of the theme song, which was issued on a tie-in album.

Only one full season was produced (plus a TV movie with the Looney Tunes and two additional appearances on a subsequent Archie/Sabrina show). Episodes were subsequently repackaged in the syndicated anthology show "The Groovie Goolies and Friends," along with various other short-lived shows produced by Filmation. This show is notable for the bumpers that led into commercial breaks, which featured the Goolies interacting with Gilligan, My Favorite Martian, and other animated characters.

Filmation made a few attempts to revive the show, but it never happened, and once the studio got sold, the characters were never utilized again. Although they didn't have the rights to the characters, the writers of the Archie TV show Riverdale made a sly reference to the Goolies by naming their resident antagonist biker gang The Ghoulies.

More info about the show is available in this insightful article, this pdf, and of course, on Wikipedia and imdb.

So here are all of the Groovie Goolies episodes, including their crossovers with Archie, Sabrina the Teenage Witch, and the Looney Tunes characters (whose voices were corrected in the fan-edit). Also includes alternate international versions of various episodes (from Czechoslovakia, France, Germany, Japan, and Spain). Plus there are CBRs and PDFs with scripts, storyboards, storybooks, art and merchandising, mp3s of the songs (in English, Czech and French) - and more!

The primary episodes came from the long out of print DVD set (plus the Sabrina and Archie sets), the video extras largely came from YouTube (some of them are long gone), many scans came from my own collection -- this stuff was amassed from a vast array of places. Thanks to everyone who unknowingly contributed.

Note: Audio commentary tracks are not playable in the archive's player, you've gotta download the files and switch to the secondary audio stream to hear them.

items.title: The Sinking of the Lusitania
items.description: The Sinking of the Lusitania, released in 1918, is an animated short film by American artist Winsor McCay. It features a short 12 minute explanation of the sinking of RMS Lusitania after it was struck by two torpedoes fired from a German U-boat. The film was one of many animated silent films published to create anti-German sentiment during World War I. McCay illustrated some 25,000 drawings for the production. The film is stylized as a documentary, informing viewers on details from the actual event, including a moment by moment recap, casualty list, and a list of prominent figures who were killed.

items.title: TMNT Season 2 Episodes - WPIX-TV 11 (10-23-1988 to 12-18-1988)
items.description:
Found in a lot of 19 used blank tapes for $50, this tape (along with another tape that will be uploaded soon) is, without a shadow of a doubt, the greatest find I've ever stumbled across anywhere. It's more the fact that I had no idea if there would be any commercial breaks retained that really kept my interest peaked. That and these two tapes are the sole reason why I purchased this 19 tape lot in the first place.

While the auctions for these tapes were going on, I managed to message the seller about the tapes being tested or not. She said that these tapes had not been tested in years, and that she pulled them out of her basement. I was really taking a blind gamble and based it solely on what was written on the tape labels.

And trust me, there were some really good titles written on there, like Transformers (from the Summer of 1985), Voltron (which ended up having no commercials at all, unfortunately), Scooby-Doo (which spanned across four tapes from varying years), and Super Sunday (which turned out to be Hanna-Barbera's Super Sunday cartoon block).

When they arrived, I expected the worst: for them to either be bootlegs, or they were taped over-the-air, but there were no commercial breaks kept in. I kept my expectations very low, in other words. Thank God I did keep them low, because I never in a million years thought that I would be keeping a record of some of the best commercials that ever aired over Saturday (or in this case, Sunday) morning television. These are truly one-of-a-kind recordings as well, because many people would have taped over these recordings with something else a long time ago, but not these people. And thank the Heavens for that!

Now, what's the reason why I've decided to upload these tapes to archive.org, and risk these encodes being scalped on eBay? These recordings are very precious to me, and to try and sell these recordings right now would be completely insane of me. I'd much rather have the public see the cream of the crop in terms of the luck of tape hunting than to sell the contents of these tapes off by themselves for monetary purposes. For those that will scalp these encodes and will put them on eBay, shame on you. But also, good for you, because that will give me a reason to never sell these original tapes for a very long time. Remember, the more that your smooth brains try and scalp these recordings, the lower the monetary value these recordings will have.

Enjoy, everyone!

~ bd

A rare collaboration between Fleischer Studios and Ub Iwerks resulted in this cartoon, based on the moderately successful Republic Pictures "Zeppelin vs. Pterodactyls" cliffhanger serials. The cartoon was shelved for half a century due to a three way legal dispute between Republic, Fleischer and Iwerks. The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences rejected Oscar nominations for Ben Burtt's sound design in the cartoon because it had not been formally released and because of the legal status.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Planet_II

Blue Planet II is a 2017 British nature documentary series on marine life produced as a co-production between the BBC Natural History Unit, BBC America, Tencent, WDR, France Télévisions and CCTV-9 in partnership with The Open University. It is a successor to The Blue Planet (2001) with naturalist Sir David Attenborough reprising his role as the narrator.

Blue Planet II was announced in 2013 and was filmed over four years in 39 countries, in more than 125 international trips. The score was composed by Hans Zimmer, Jacob Shea and David Fleming. The rock band Radiohead reworked their 2011 song "Bloom" with Zimmer for the series.

Blue Planet II debuted on 29 October 2017 and was simultaneously cast on BBC One, BBC One HD and BBC Earth, making it the first natural history series to premiere on the same day in the UK, Nordic regions, Europe and in Asia. In the US, it premiered on January 20, 2018, as part of a five-network simulcast on BBC America, AMC, IFC, Sundance, and WE tv.

Blue Planet II received acclaim. It had the highest viewing figures of any television program in the UK in 2017, and was so widely watched in China that it reportedly caused internet problems. It is credited with increasing public and political interest in issues affecting marine life, in particular marine plastic pollution, which was dubbed "the Blue Planet effect".

It won several awards: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Planet_II#Awards_and_nominations

Read the rest of the information HERE: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Planet_II

Blue Planet II, which accompanies an epic 7-part series on BBC1, is a ground-breaking new look at the richness and variety of underwater life across our planet. With over 200 breath-taking photographs and stills from the BBC Natural History Unit's spectacular footage, each chapter of Blue Planet II brings to life a different habitat of the oceanic world. Episode Descriptions:

1"One Ocean"Jonathan Smith29 October 201714.01
Animals featured include bottlenose dolphins that surf and rub themselves in corals in the Red Sea, smart tuskfish that use coral to break open clam shells, large packs of giant trevallies hunting tern chicks in atolls in the Indian Ocean, false killer whales joining a pack of bottlenose dolphins in New Zealand, a female kobudai changing its sex to male, orca and humpback whales feasting in large schools of herring in Norway and walruses trying to rest on the melting ice in the Arctic to escape polar bears.
2"The Deep"Orla Doherty5 November 201713.97
The depths of the ocean are among the most difficult conditions in the world. The depths of Antarctica host diverse endemic creatures. In other oceans, giant tunicate – pyrosome, swordfish, cock-eyed squid and barreleyes are specially adapted to dark conditions, and large Humboldt squids hunt lanternfish then cannibalize one another. The deep sea anglerfish and dragonfish attracts prey, and fangtooths eat fish and squid. In the deep, a sperm whale carcass attracts many scavengers, such as bluntnose sixgill sharks, spider crabs, rock crabs, and osedax; as well as the scavenger's predators, including silver scabbardfish. Also features shrimps living in a Venus' flower basket sponge, swimming pools of brine in the Gulf of Mexico, and the life found in the Mariana Trench, including the snailfish.
3"Coral Reefs"Jonathan Smith12 November 201713.45
Coral reefs are a large habitat created by tiny creatures called coral polyps. Features broadclub cuttlefish searching prey, coral trout cooperatively hunting with octopus, Green sea turtles in Borneo cleaned by surgeonfish and blennies, bottlenose dolphins playing, a bobbit worm hunting in the sands of the reef, a family of saddleback clownfish transporting a shell on which to lay their eggs, and marbled groupers breeding in French Polynesia while grey reef sharks attack.
4"Big Blue"John Ruthven19 November 201713.11
A large school of spinner dolphins chase lanternfish with yellowfin tuna, sailfish and the mobula ray, sperm whales with their calves hunting squid, young sea turtles find refuge at flotsam, blue sharks scavenge a whale carcass with the world's largest predatory fish, the great white shark. A Portuguese man o' war floats in the current waiting for small fish, whale sharks breed in the Galápagos Islands along with hammerhead and silky sharks, and wandering albatrosses raising their chicks. Highlights the effects of plastic on marine life, with a short-finned pilot whale family mourning a calf that died after ingesting milk contaminated with plastic particles.
5"Green Seas"Kathryn Jeffs26 November 201712.62
Within kelp forests, starfish release their eggs, which are consumed by sea cucumbers and sea pens. Common octopus escape from pyjama sharks by hiding inside shells; Garibaldi hide from torpedo rays and try to protect their patches of seaweed from grazers and from a plague of sea urchins, whose numbers are kept in check by sea otters. In Australia, green sea turtles graze on seagrass beds and are chased by tiger sharks. Other inhabitants of the seagrass beds are spider crabs coming to molt with protection from a short-tail stingray, giant cuttlefish mating, and weedy seadragon fathers carrying eggs. In the mangrove roots of North Australia, a zebra mantis shrimp hunts small fish for his mate. A large pack of common dolphins, California sea lions and humpback whales feasting in school of anchovies, themselves feeding on phytoplankton, in Monterey Bay.
6"Coasts"Miles Barton3 December 201711.45
Animals featured include thousands of olive ridley sea turtles that come up to land to lay their eggs; Galápagos sea lion catching yellowfin tuna in the shallow bay of the coast; rock pool creatures including predators like starfish, sea anemones and clingfishes that prey on limpets and bivalves; a chain moray eel and an octopus hunt Sally Lightfoot crabs in Brazil, puffins and common murres avoiding arctic skuas, Pacific leaping blennies making their home on land; a colony of king penguins crossing a colony of fiercely territorial southern elephant seals; and large groups of spinner sharks and blacktip sharks off the coast of Palm Beach, Florida.
7"Our Blue Planet"Orla Doherty, Will Ridgeon10 December 201711.91
Examining the role of human anthropogenic activity on the oceans. Microplastics and pollution are an increasing problem for the world's seas, threatening the lives of marine life and ultimately affecting the ecosystem. Can humans reverse their activity to protect the seas and the wildlife that inhabit it?

(I was extremely lucky to read his review only a few hours after he posted it!)

So, you need to download the 6.5 Gigabyte file again: and delete the older copy.

In 1860, as the American Experiment threatened to explode into a bloody civil war, there were as many as four hundred thousand slave-owners in the United States, and almost four million slaves. The nation was founded upon the idea that all men are created equal and endowed by their creator with the inalienable rights of life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness. The nation would pay a bloody cost for denying that right to more than twelve percent of its population. But when slavery was first brought to America's shores, this war, and even the nation it tore apart, was centuries in the future. 

With incredibly detailed historical reenactments, expert commentary and the stories of slavery told through first-hand accounts, this is an epic struggle 400 years in the making. A journey into the past like none other. This is the story of these men and women who by their hands laid the foundation of what would become the most powerful nation on Earth. Join us as we rise...UP FROM SLAVERY.
